excerpt: If $w_T>0$ then $\alpha_i\ge w_T>0$ for every $i\in T$, and $\sum_i\alpha_i\log\alpha_i=\sum_Tw_T\sum_{i\in T}\log\alpha_i$, the sums running over sets with $w_T>0$. Hence the left side equals $\sum_{w_T>0}w_T\log\bigl(\prod_{i\in T}\alpha_i/w_T\bigr)$, which by concavity of the logarithm is at most $\log\sum_T\prod_{i\in T}\alpha_i$. In the expansion of $(\sum_i\alpha_i)^m$ each product $\prod_{i\in T}\alpha_i$ with $\abs T=m$ occurs $m!$ times and all other terms are nonnegative, so $\sum_T\prod_{i\in T}\alpha_i\le(\sum_i\alpha_i)^m/m!=m^m/m!$, because $\sum_i\alpha_i=m$.
derivation: Rewrite the left side as sum w_T log(prod_{i in T}alpha_i/w_T). Concavity of log gives log sum_T prod alpha_i. In (sum alpha_i)^m every distinct m-subset monomial occurs m! times, all other terms nonnegative, and sum alpha_i=m.
